studies.label: Randomized feedback-sequence crossover: product improvement

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 169), Method: Participants; repeated exposure to both conditions is described on PDF p. 8 (printed p. 172), Procedure, and shown in Figure 3 on PDF p. 9 (printed p. 173).
counts_source.quote: Hence, the final sample size of 62 participants provided adequate statistical power for the primary analyses, though correlational results should be interpreted with caution due to slightly reduced power.

arms.name: Standard GenAI feedback (ChatGPT-4)
arms.description: General-purpose ChatGPT-4 supplies open-ended responses to general prompts, supporting unstructured exploration. All participants experience this condition in the crossover. The analyzed count denotes the final study cohort exposed to this condition; outcome-specific valid-pair counts are not printed. Sources: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 169), Participants and GenAI feedback conditions; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 172), Procedure.

arms.name: Personalised GenAI feedback (Mr. Ranedeer)
arms.description: GPT-4-based Mr. Ranedeer uses configured knowledge level, learning style, tone and communication style to generate a personalised learning plan and adapt feedback and scaffolding. All participants experience this condition in the crossover; its analyzed count is the same final cohort as in the standard condition. Sources: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 169), Participants and GenAI feedback conditions; PDF p. 8 (printed p. 172), Procedure; Appendix Tables A1-A2, PDF pp. 20-21 (printed pp. 184-185).

studies.task: Using the assigned GenAI tool, propose three original and useful product improvements for a stuffed bunny and a portable coffee maker, and submit the final responses in Microsoft Word (PDF pp. 7-8, printed pp. 171-172, CPS performance and Procedure).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4 (standard) and Mr. Ranedeer (personalised), both based on GPT-4 architecture
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 169), GenAI feedback conditions. The document does not specify a release year or exact model snapshot.

preregistration.where: No preregistration or designated primary outcome is identified in the complete article or its appendix.

studies.shared_sample: Probable shared sample with c041, Effects of Personalized Generative AI on Student Creativity: Evidence from Creative Performance, Self-efficacy, and Attention Allocation (DOI 10.1007/978-981-95-4499-8_31), as flagged in forms/c246.json, sample_overlap. Matching sample descriptions and identical creativity arm means and SDs were checked on c246 PDF pp. 4-5 and 11 (printed pp. 168-169 and 175) and c041 PDF pp. 4 and 8 (printed pp. 379 and 383). This is an inference, not confirmed participant reuse; exact overlap remains unknown. c246 reports its own effect sizes, which differ from c041 and are retained here.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Novelty of the solutions. Two trained raters, blinded to condition, independently rated all solutions on a five-point Likert scale from worst to best. Solutions were presented in random order and final scores averaged across raters. Domain-expert credentials and aggregation across each participant’s requested solutions are not stated (PDF p. 8, printed p. 172, Measures: CPS performance).

sources.locator: PDF p. 11 (printed p. 175), Table 2, Originality row. Columns: Standard mean (SD), Personalised mean (SD), z, p, Cohen’s r, 95% CI for Cohen’s r.

sources.quote: The 95% confidence intervals (CI) for Cohen’s r are provided in brackets.

estimates.notes: Full-sample condition comparison using a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test (PDF p. 10, printed p. 174, Data analysis; PDF p. 11, printed p. 175, Results). The personalised condition has a lower printed mean than the standard condition. The published signs are transcribed without reversal. The paper does not define the sign convention or standardizer for Cohen’s r. Its confidence limits are recorded in paper_effect; ci_level is expressed as the printed percentage. Table 2 does not print outcome-specific participant counts or valid-pair counts, so the contrast counts remain null; the final cohort count is retained only in the study and arm records. The paper specifies averaging raters but not averaging solutions, leaving unit, sd_level and the basis of the reported uncertainty unresolved. No first-round-only results, raw mean difference, paired-difference SD or participant-level SE are printed. Original numeric precision is preserved in the source-row quote.

not_extracted.what: Self-efficacy with the assigned GenAI tool
not_extracted.reason: Self-reported confidence rather than creativity scored on produced solutions; administered before each task and used as a covariate. PDF p. 8 (printed p. 172), Measures: Self-efficacy; PDF p. 10 (printed p. 174), Data analysis.

Frequency of disregarding AI feedback is an engagement/process measure coded from responses following AI messages, rather than a creativity or diversity score on the produced solutions. PDF p. 9 (printed p. 173), Coding scheme: Feedback uptake; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 175), Table 3.

Frequency of directly inserting AI content is an engagement/process measure rather than a creativity or diversity score on the produced solutions. PDF p. 9 (printed p. 173), Coding scheme: Feedback uptake; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 175), Table 3.

Frequency of critically evaluating and expanding AI suggestions is coded as feedback-uptake behaviour; it does not score the final solutions for creativity or diversity. PDF p. 9 (printed p. 173), Coding scheme: Feedback uptake; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 175), Table 3.

Total coded feedback-uptake frequency is a process measure, not a count of distinct creative solutions or a score on their creativity or diversity. PDF p. 9 (printed p. 173), Coding scheme: Feedback uptake; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 175), Table 3.

not_extracted.what: Within-condition feedback-uptake correlations and regressions predicting quality, elaboration and originality
not_extracted.reason: Associations with observed post-assignment uptake behaviours within each condition, rather than randomized contrasts between AI configurations. The backward regressions use uptake predictors and prior-experience/self-efficacy covariates. PDF p. 10 (printed p. 174), Data analysis; PDF pp. 11-12 (printed pp. 175-176), Tables 4-6.

not_extracted.what: Interaction-behaviour frequencies: generate new ideas without interaction, build upon GenAI’s idea, develop new ideas through interaction, plan for personalised learning, coordinate task/provide substantive information, request clarification/solution, negotiate inconsistencies, task-irrelevant discourse, and total interactions
not_extracted.reason: Counts of categories of conversation behaviour during the task. They classify student responses to AI messages and are not reported as counts of distinct submitted ideas or output creativity/diversity scores. PDF pp. 9-10 (printed pp. 173-174), Interaction behaviours and Table 1; PDF p. 13 (printed p. 177), Table 7.

not_extracted.what: Lag-sequential behavioural transitions and their adjusted residuals
not_extracted.reason: Within-condition temporal associations between interaction behaviours and feedback uptake are process analyses, not randomized effects on creative output. PDF p. 10 (printed p. 174), Data analysis; PDF p. 13 (printed p. 177), Figure 4 and associated text.

not_extracted.what: Task completion time by feedback condition
not_extracted.reason: Task duration is a process/resource measure rather than creativity or diversity scored on produced solutions. PDF p. 8 (printed p. 172), Procedure.

open_items: Outcome-specific participant and valid-pair counts are not printed in Table 2 (PDF p. 11, printed p. 175). The final study sample is reported in Participants, but does not confirm the number of people contributing to each Wilcoxon calculation. All contrast count fields remain null.

The unit of the Table 2 means, SDs and tests is unresolved. The paper says scores were averaged across raters but does not specify aggregation across the requested solutions (PDF p. 8, printed p. 172, CPS performance). unit and sd_level remain null and se_basis is unclear; participant-level precision is not established.

No first-round-only outcomes, paired-difference SDs, within-person correlations, or participant-level SEs are reported. The formula and sign convention for Cohen’s r and the method used for its confidence intervals are not specified (PDF pp. 10-11, printed pp. 174-175).

An aggregate number randomized before any exclusions is not separately printed. Assignment was to feedback sequence, not to exclusive AI conditions; the study and condition n_randomized fields remain null. The sequence sizes printed in the procedure/diagram do not resolve whether any participants were excluded before the final sample.

The product/task order in the second sequence is ambiguous: Procedure says the other half completed the tasks in reverse order, whereas Figure 3 labels PIT 1 then PIT 2 in both branches and reverses feedback condition (PDF pp. 8-9, printed pp. 172-173).

Probable participant overlap with c041 requires confirmation of cohort identity and exact shared-person count before treating the reports as independent. The matching sample descriptions and creativity means/SDs support the screening flag; the reported effect sizes differ between documents.
The AI release year and exact GPT-4 snapshot are not specified (PDF p. 5, printed p. 169, GenAI feedback conditions); ai_tool.year remains null.
notes: Extraction completed against the local journal PDF. The entire markdown conversion, including references and appendix, was read in chunks. All figures were inspected from embedded PDF images; tables and all quoted numbers were checked using PyMuPDF page text, with text-strategy table extraction also checked for Table 2. Figure 3 explicitly states “Random assignment of feedback sequence”; the paired AI-design contrasts therefore meet the randomized-order requirement. Figures contain no additional eligible outcome statistics. All three eligible full-sample contrasts are in Table 2; no first-round, across-people diversity, or after-AI outcome is reported. The same participants experience both conditions; their counts must not be added. No effect sizes, standard deviations, standard errors, mean differences or sample sizes were calculated, and no results from c041 were substituted.
